title: An Afternoon in the Archive
paragraphs: During an afternoon at a community archive, a class examined records of ordinary experiences. Some came from personal journals, while others resembled reports or scenes from fiction. The students agreed that useful evidence could come from a quiet incident as well as a surprising one.

The opening pages introduced several situations worth examining carefully. Without water, the leaves will wither and turn brown. The council will initiate a study of traffic near the school. We must modify the design so that the shelves fit the smaller room. Running too soon could aggravate the ankle injury.

The remaining pages widened the discussion with additional observations. The shop will deduct the discount from the final price. The principal may expel students who repeatedly commit serious offenses. Use a spoon to blend the flour and water into a smooth paste. Workers will raze the unsafe warehouse before building the new station.

By the end of the discussion, the students had learned why careful reading requires more than a quick judgment. A useful interpretation must fit the details of the situation. They chose a conclusion that acknowledged differences among the accounts, and they left readers with a question: which observation most strongly supports your view, and what might change your mind?

targets.definition: to dry up and lose freshness
to cause an activity or process to begin
to make a limited change to something
to make a problem or injury worse
to subtract an amount from a total
to force someone or something to leave
